text: . Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. US President Donald Trump has reportedly rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end hostilities in the region, even as Iran awaits an official US response to its plans. An American Newspaper reported about Trump’s views, quoting US officials.Iran had earlier proposed a seven-day process under which hostilities would end on all fronts, while the United States would lift its blockade on Iranian ports, release frozen Iranian funds and waive oil sanctions. The Strait of Hormuz would then be reopened as per this proposal.Iraq is seeking an exemption for some of its airports from the USA’s sanctions policy affecting Iranian airlines. Iraqi PM’s Media Office has posted on X that their government is conducting direct dialogue with the American side to exempt some Iraqi airports from these measures, in a manner that allows the resumption of air travel, for humanitarian reasons related to treatment, study, religious visits, and civilian interests. The move comes after Iranian flights were suspended at Iraqi airports amid the US threat of sanctions against companies and airports providing services to Iranian carriers.Earlier today, Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition said that it had intercepted two ballistic missiles and two drones launched by the Houthis towards Saudi Arabia. The coalition said the missiles were headed towards Khamis Mushait and the drones towards Riyadh. The latest attacks came hours after the military chiefs of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkiye met in Riyadh to review threats facing Saudi Arabia. The three countries had signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement on August 7, 2026, stipulating that an armed attack on any one of the three countries would be regarded as an attack on all three.

The Ministry of Education, in coordination with the External Affairs Ministry is organizing a two day Bharat Innovates Exposition from today at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi to showcase India’s Deep-Tech innovations as a lead up to and alongside the 18th BRICS Summit 2026. The Exposition is showcasing 37 India’s Deep-Tech startups and ventures alligning with the theme of India’s BRICS Chairship Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The event is providing participating innovators an opportunity to network with CEOs, investors, business leaders and industry representatives from BRICS member countries. Ministry of Eduaction said that the event will facilitate opportunities for Business to Business engagements, technology partnerships, investment discussions, business linkages and international market access.

. Reserve Bank of India Deputy Governor Rohit Jain today said technology was no longer merely an enabler of banking but was increasingly becoming part of banks’ risk architecture.Addressing the 13th SBI Banking & Economics Conclave 2026 in Mumbai, Mr Jain highlighted the growing role of technology in banking and said technology is now embedded in almost every critical banking function, from core banking and payments to customer onboarding, credit assessment, fraud monitoring, and even regulatory reporting.On artificial intelligence, Jain said it could improve customer service, fraud detection, risk assessment and productivity, but could also amplify errors and influence decisions related to credit, fraud alerts, customer access, pricing and service delivery.Mr Jain that boards and senior management must have sufficient technological understanding to question assumptions, assess dependencies and ensure that resilience arrangements are properly tested.

. Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri has emphasised the urgency of UNSC reform to ensure greater voice and representation for developing countries. Delivering India’s statement at the 50th Annual Meeting of Foreign Ministers of the Group of 77 (G77) at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly in New York, Mr Misri called for collective efforts to enable the Global South to move from being rule-takers to rule-shapers. He also underscored the continued relevance of the G77 in advancing people-centric and development-oriented multilateralism.

. The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) facilitated the flag-off of a one MT consignment of GI-tagged Gulbarga Tur Dal from Karnataka to the Maldives. The consignment, exported yesterday by M/s Silken Global Exports and Imports, Mysuru, through its Farmer Producer Organisation (FPO)-led brand, will be transported to the Maldives by sea. The Ministry of Commerce and Industry said that the initiative is aimed at expanding international markets for India’s GI-tagged agricultural products and strengthening the participation of FPO-led brands in agri exports.It added that a key feature of the export-linked value chain is improved price realisation for farmers, which enables farmers to realise 82 rupees per kg against prevailing market price of 60 rupees per kg. It provides FPOs an opportunity to participate more closely in export-oriented value chains and connect producers with international markets. The Ministry further noted that the export is expected to pave the way for regular shipments of Gulbarga Tur Dal to the Maldives, creating sustained market opportunities for producers and exporters from Karnataka. The initiative is also expected to support greater value realisation for farmers and enable FPOs and farmers to integrate more closely with export-oriented value chains.

. In Bangladesh, Durga Puja is celebrated every year with devotion, religious fervour and enthusiasm.  This year, Durga Puja will be celebrated from 16th to 21st October. With only a few weeks left for the festival, preparations are in full swing across Bangladesh.Preparations for Durga Puja are also clearly visible at Dhakeshwari Temple, one of the prominent religious sites of the Hindu community in Bangladesh. A meeting of leaders from around 70 district and metropolitan committees of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad was held at the temple premises today. The meeting reviewed preparations for Durga Puja across the country, as well as the prevailing communal situation.The meeting was chaired by Bashudeb Dhar, President of the Bangladesh Puja Udjapan Parishad. Central leaders of the organisation, along with representatives of various district and metropolitan committees, took part in the meeting and discussed different aspects related to the preparations for the festival.Meanwhile, other preparations for Durga Puja have also gained momentum at the temple premises. Cleaning, painting and decoration work is underway, with people associated with the organisation actively engaged in preparations for the festival.People are also engaged in making arrangements for the Puja. Members of the organising committees were seen collecting contributions from devotees and others at the temple premises to support the arrangements for the festival.Durga Puja is not only a religious festival but also a major cultural celebration. A large number of women and girls were seen rehearsing cultural programmes to be presented during the Puja at the Dhakeshwari Temple premises. One of the artists said that preparations for such performances take at least 15 days.The preparations for the festival are also visible at the shops in and around the temple premises. A large number of people were seen purchasing various items required for the Puja.Apart from Dhakeshwari Temple, preparations for Durga Puja are also in full swing at other temples in Dhaka. At Shri Shri Ramna Kali Temple, artisans are busy making idols of various deities for the upcoming Durga Puja.Idol-making is a long and painstaking process. The basic framework is first prepared using paddy straw and wood. The artisans then carefully shape the idols with clay. The process requires considerable skill, precision and craftsmanship.Along with Goddess Durga, idols of Lord Ganesha, Goddess Saraswati and Lord Shiva, among others, are also prepared for the Puja. Idols of animals and birds representing the mounts of the deities are also crafted with great skill and attention to detail.Once the basic structure and shape of the idols are completed, the artisans work on the finer details. This is followed by painting and final decoration. Artisans are now busy giving the idols their final touches ahead of the festival.AAs Durga Puja draws closer, preparations at temples across Bangladesh are gathering further momentum. From cleaning and decoration to idol-making, cultural rehearsals and the purchase of Puja items, preparations for Durga Puja are progressing with enthusiasm across Bangladesh.

. Russian attacks across Ukraine have killed at least four people today as Moscow and Kyiv intensify their aerial warfare.Russia has attacked Ukraine with cruise and ballistic missiles, powerful glide bombs and jet-powered drones while front-line progress has largely slowed. Russia’s Ministry of Defence said that its attack on Kyiv had damaged a data centre that supported both cellphone internet services and Starlink satellite communication systems.Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy today warned it’s partners that Russia is escalating every single day. He said that if Moscow had chosen to make its strikes more brutal, the international community must respond with stronger measures to prevent the war from spreading further.Earlier this week, Zelenskyy urged countries at the UN to further restrict Russia’s access to revenue through sanctions and trade bans, arguing that cutting Moscow’s income would limit its ability to sustain the war.Meanwhile, Ukraine has continued its long-range drone campaign against targets inside Russia, including oil refineries and industrial facilities.

Indian men’s and women’s compound archery teams made it to the semifinals of their respective categories at the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya today.The men’s trio of Sahil Jadhav, Ganesh Mani Ratnam, and Kushal Dalal beat Bhutan 235-232 by the narrowest of margins to seal a semifinal clash against South Korea.The women’s team of Chikitha Taniparthi, Jyothi Surekha Vennam, and Prithika Pradeep beat Kazakhstan 233-230 to seal a semifinal clash against South Korea.Coming to surfing, India also got some good news out of the women’s shortboard event as both Sugar Shanti Gayen and Kamali Prakash made it to the third round. Sugar Shanti beat Chen Wan-yu of Chinese Taipei with a score of 7.33. Kamali Prakash beat Singapore’s Camille Marie Spaccarotella, scoring 7.57. The quarterfinal will take place tomorrow.India have so far won 30 medals comprising four gold, 12 silver and 14 bronze medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.

In the FIDE Chess Olympiad, reigning World Classical Chess Champion Dommaraju Gukesh secured a clutch win to help India beat overnight joint-topper Germany 2.5-1.5 in the ninth round of the men’s Open section, moving up to second position in the standings.With this win, India roared back into title contention as they are in a good position to challenge table-toppers Uzbekistan for the title. In the crucial clash on Table 2, R. Praggnanandhaa, Arjun Erigaisi and Nihal Sarin were held to draws on the first three boards before Gukesh secured the lone victory of the match against Germany.In the women’s section, B Savitha Shri’s incredible run of seven successive wins came to an end, but she remained unbeaten after a draw against Karimova Guldona of Uzbekistan on the top table. Koneru Humpy was held by top Uzbek Afruza Khamdamova, but Women’s World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh and Ventika Agrawal won their games to secure a 3-1 win for India.The victory took them to 15 points from nine rounds as they shared the second spot with Kazakhstan and Mongolia. Armenia went down 1-3 to leaders China, while Mongolia drew 2-2 with Kazakhstan.

. India won the silver medal in the women’s 50-metre rifle three positions team event at the Asian Games. The trio of Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa Vinod and Ashi Chouksey scored 1,763 points, finishing behind China, which won gold with a Games record of 1,773 points. Kazakhstan took bronze with 1,754 points.In the individual final, Tilottama Sen narrowly missed a podium finish, securing fourth place with 337.3 points, while Vidarsa Vinod finished fifth with 327.4 points. China’s Jiayu Han won the gold.

Both the Indian men’s and women’s Kabaddi teams today won gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 in Japan.The Indian men’s Kabaddi team clinched gold, beating Iran 40-34 at the Asian Games. The Indian women’s team also edged out Iran in a tense final clash, winning the contest by a 37-34 margin. India has made a strong medal haul at the Asian Games today, adding seven medals across Kabaddi, athletics, shooting and squash. Now India are currently placed 10th in the medal standings and its overall tally has reached 30 with four gold, twelve silver and fourteen bronze.In athletics, Tajinderpal Singh Toor won the silver medal in the men’s shot put with a throw of 20.64 meters. Sawan Barwal bagged silver in the men’s marathon ending India’s 44-year wait for a podium finish in the discipline, clocking 2 hours, 11 minutes and 37 seconds. His performance marked a personal best and a new national record. In shooting, Tilottama Sen, Vidarsa K. Vinod and Ashi Chouksey secured silver in the women’s 50-metre rifle three-position team event, scoring 1,763 points. Prachi Chaudhary win bronze in women’s 400m with a timing of 53.21 seconds. In mixed doubles squash, Joshna Chinappa and Velavan Senthilkumar bagged bronze.President Droupadi Murmu has extended her greetings to the Indian Men’s Kabaddi Team on winning the Gold Medal at the 2026 Asian Games. In a social media post, the President highlighted that with both the Men’s and Women’s teams securing top honours, India has achieved a historic golden double sweep in Kabaddi. The President praised the athletes, stating that this twin victory showcases the team members’ exceptional skill, composure, resilience, and outstanding teamwork that paved the way for India’s triumph.Prime Minister Narendra Modi has congratulated men’s and women’s kabaddi team for securing gold medals in the Asian Games 2026. In a social media post, the Prime Minister said that the country is proud of its kabaddi champions. He noted that the team displayed remarkable courage, composure and teamwork. He wished players of both teams for their future endeavours.

In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today stated that the surgical strike by the Indian Army on the terrorist hideouts in Pakistan demonstrated a new example of India’s counter-terrorism policy to the world. Addressing the nation in his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani, Mr Modi said India is set to mark the tenth anniversary of the surgical strike tomorrow (28th September). He said the world was astonished to see the manner in which brave Indian soldiers crossed the Line of Control to take action against terrorism.Prime Minister Modi said the surgical strike was India’s decisive response to the long-standing pain the nation had endured due to terrorist attacks. He stated that over the past decade – from the Balakot airstrike to ‘Operation Sindoor ’, India has repeatedly sent the message that terrorist strikes will be met with a befitting response.Mr Modi recounted that there was a time when serial blasts had become a common occurrence in the country. He said many lives were lost in the serial blasts in Delhi on 13th September, 2008. The 26/11 attack took place just a few weeks later in Mumbai. He highlighted that today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and country is witnessing the results of that.Prime Minister Modi said this year also marks 25 years since the 9/11 terrorist attacks. He said that the highest number of victims at the World Trade Center in the US, after Americans, were Indians. He recalled paying homage to those innocent citizens during his US visit after becoming Prime Minister in 2014. He once again extended his condolences to the bereaved families on behalf of crores of Indian citizens.Touching upon the topic of the ongoing census, Mr Modi said the first phase of this exercise is nearly complete across all States and Union Territories. Data of over 32 crore families has already been recorded. Work is currently underway also in the remote, snow-clad regions of Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttarakhand.The Prime Minister noted that many inspiring experiences have emerged from these areas. In Uttarakhand, the census process began in the village of Mana in Chamoli, which is known as the country’s first village. Prime Minister Modi said the process there started with 83-year-old Purnima Rawat. In Bagori village of Uttarkashi, Hardev Singh Rana, who runs a homestay, entered his details himself using digital means.Mr Modi emphasised that the census is a national responsibility for all. He added that the facility to self-register census details is very convenient and people can register information about themselves and their family from their mobiles themselves. Along with Hindi, this facility is available in 16 languages. The Prime Minister asked people to visit the census online portal, se.census.gov.in, and log in with their mobile number, enter location, fill in details regarding their family and submit the information.The Prime Minister said the entire process takes about 15 to 20 minutes. No document needs to be uploaded for this. After submitting the information, people will receive a special ID, which can be shared with the census enumerator when they pay a visit. After the information is verified, it becomes part of the census record.Prime Minister Modi informed that so far, more than 2 crore 60 lakh people have already entered their details on the census portal via mobile, completing the self-enumeration. He said accurate information about citizens and their families helps create a precise picture of the country’s future.The Prime Minister said today marks the 100th birth anniversary of the revered late Ashok Singhal, who was the former International Working President of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad. He called him a great personality who dedicated his entire life to culture, society, and the nation. Born on 27th September, 1926, in Agra, Ashok Singhal led a life as an ascetic even though living amidst society. Prime Minister Modi said the very direction and energy he imparted to the Ram Janmabhoomi movement veritably resulted in the magnificent temple in Ayodhya today.Alongside the Ram Mandir movement, Ashok Singhal also waged a major battle against social discrimination and inequality. Mr Modi offered his tributes on the occasion of his birth centenary.The Prime Minister said the nation began this year with a grand celebration of national pride, which is the Somnath Swabhiman Parv. He said that Mahmud of Ghazni had demolished the Somnath Temple for the first time a thousand years ago in 1026 AD. He highlighted that the Somnath Temple still stands in all its grandeur by the sea, bestowing the blessing of immortality upon India. He added that this is why the Somnath Swabhiman Parv was celebrated with immense pride this year.Mr Modi mentioned that he brought up this topic in Mann Ki Baat today for a special reason. In 1026 AD, when Ghazni destroyed the Somnath Temple, the famous Sun Temple in Modhera, Gujarat, was also attacked and destroyed the same year. He said a thousand years have passed since the destruction of the Modhera temple as well, whereas the temple had been built just a year ago. King Bhimdev had got it built in 1025.The Prime Minister remarked that King Bhimdev the First not only confronted the forces of Ghazni but also had the Modhera Sun Temple rebuilt within a short time. He opined that it is because of this very resilience that the Somnath Temple, too, was rebuilt every time despite facing repeated destruction.Mr Modi said attacks on the Modhera Sun Temple did not cease later either. Alauddin Khilji later destroyed this temple once again. Emphasising that the people of India do not worship the Sun solely through architecture and temples, he said, for us, the Sun also signifies light, energy, science, and the inspiration for continuity. He pointed out that this is why Modhera is known today not just for its Sun Temple, but has become the country’s first ‘Surya Gram’, that is, Solar Village.Modhera now runs entirely on solar energy, setting an example of sustainability for the nation.Several attractions and amenities for tourists have also been introduced in Modhera. The Modhera Dance Festival is held in January, following Makar Sankranti. It features magnificent performances of India’s cultural and classical dances. He urged people to visit Modhera at least once and witness this glorious Indian heritage.In today’s Mann Ki Baat, Mr Modi also spoke about a unique initiative underway in Manapparai, Tiruchirappalli, Tamil Nadu, to connect with the country’s past. He mentioned A. Selvaraju, associated with the Department of Tamil Studies at a college, who is spearheading this effort.During a lecture, he learned about some ancient sculptures from a student. He planned a field visit following a discussion on the subject. During this visit, he discovered several sculptures and ancient temples at various locations. Mr Modi said this is a fascinating way to connect with the past and understand the country’s heritage even better.The Prime Minister also mentioned Mahatma Gandhi’s birth anniversary, which will be celebrated on the 2nd of October. He said cleanliness is one of many guiding principles for life given by Bapu. Citing several examples of initiatives to maintain cleanliness, Mr Modi said young people in Madhya Pradesh are working to clean up a river. Similarly, in Andhra Pradesh, youth are cleaning up old stepwells and wells, helping to restore India’s ancient heritage.In Mumbai, some young people are taking the initiative to keep beaches clean. Mr Modi said that in Delhi, children and youth are raising awareness about segregating waste and maintaining cleanliness in their surroundings. In West Bengal, students are collaborating with locals to clean up market areas at picnic spots.The Prime Minister pointed out that all these efforts start with a single individual first, and a movement grows when others join in. He said this is what Jan Bhagidari is all about. He stated that cleanliness is the most beautiful tribute the nation can pay to Mahatma Gandhi.Mr Modi stressed that entire ecosystems are strengthened when the environment is protected. He added that some initiatives taking place in various parts of the country are beautifully highlighting this sentiment. He gave the example of Sonai Rupai Wildlife Sanctuary in Assam. There was a time when elephants used to inhabit this area, but as human interference on forest land increased, the elephants moved away.Prime Minister Modi was pleased to note that this land was cleared of encroachment three years ago, and the results have been remarkable. Elephants have returned to this place again, and herds of elephants are once again being spotted in areas where they had not been active for years.Mr Modi also spoke about the initiative in Assam itself to save the Pygmy Hog. The Pygmy Hog’s very existence was under threat once upon a time. A conservation programme was launched with just six Pygmy Hogs, and they were reintroduced into the wild. Grasslands were also curated for their living. The Prime Minister expressed happiness that thanks to this programme, the Pygmy Hog population has risen to over 190.Mentioning the human bond with nature, Prime Minister Modi spoke about an inspiring example in the Sundarbans of West Bengal, where some women from Jharkhali are creating mangrove forests. Most of them are women who lost their husbands to tiger attacks. Mr Modi remarked that after losing their husbands, they found a means of livelihood within the Sundarbans itself.The mangroves they have planted are now serving as a natural protective shield for their villages, while also providing them with an income. Mr Modi urged everyone to conserve the environment, respect the balance of nature, and safeguard its diversity.Prime Minister Modi noted that millions of young people across the country have recently taken a significant resolve against substance abuse and drugs, under the Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan. They have vowed to stay away from drugs and have also taken up the responsibility of spreading this message to others. Mr Modi said Nasha Mukt Yuva Abhiyan will run for 100 weeks. It includes volunteers from MY Bharat, and youth associated with the NSS are part of this.He added that in just the last few days, thousands of pledge ceremonies and awareness programmes have taken place across the country. He appreciated the ‘Nasha-Mukti Ka Sandesh’ initiative under which the nation’s youth are propagating this message in their own language and in their own way.Mr Modi had urged young people through ‘Mann Ki Baat’ to join this campaign using their creativity. He expressed delight that thousands of youth have stepped forward in response to this call. Various competitions, including anthem, slogan writing, and street plays, have been organised on the ‘MY Bharat’ platform.Similarly, young people are sharing creative content on social media using the hashtag – NashaMuktYuva. Prime Minister Modi noted that in essence, the message, the medium, and the driving energy behind it all come from the youth themselves. He added that in the coming days, activities such as health check-ups and meditation camps will also be conducted as part of this campaign.Mr Modi urged people to look around them amidst the festive celebrations and support people who are trying to break free from addiction. He said everyone must work together to advance the resolve of a drug-free youth and a Viksit Bharat.On Sports, the Prime Minister said he had announced a talent hunt campaign for Sports from the Red Fort this time. He said it is essential to reach out to villages and towns to discover sporting talent to ensure India continues to perform well.  He spoke about Rajinder Singh from Punjab, who was part of the team that won the gold medal in hockey at the 1980 Olympics. He also shone at the 1982 World Cup. In 2001, India won the Men’s Junior World Cup title for the first time, whereas in 2003, the country clinched the Senior Asia Cup title. Rajinder Singh was the coach in both these tournaments. Now, he is pursuing his passion through the Round Glass Hockey Academy.Mr Modi said the Hockey coach has a very clear focus on identifying children in villages that lack access to excellent coaching facilities. Lauding Rajinder Singh’s dedication, the Prime Minister added that many players are securing spots at India’s junior and senior levels through such initiatives.On One District One Product, the Prime Minister said Amla, the Indian gooseberry, is now becoming a source of new possibilities in Pratapgarh, Uttar Pradesh. He said farmers in Pratapgarh have been growing Amla for generations. He further stated that One District One Product has boosted local entrepreneurs involved in the Amla trade.Today, around 100 units for Amla processing are operational in Pratapgarh, with women connected with self-help groups playing a significant role. Mr Modi said the Savitri Phule Self-Help Group from Devgarh Kamasi village is producing Amla candy, preserves, and juice. Access to new markets through the ODOP scheme has also increased income.Similarly, women of Vindhyavasini Self-Help Group are producing many items like Amla pickle and digestive powder. These women received help in guise of machinery for processing and access to loan facilities.Prime Minister Modi remarked that every region of the country possesses some unique speciality, be it a specific fruit, a traditional art form, or a unique skill. He said the One District, One Product campaign aims to promote these very specialities. He further said the endeavour is to ensure that the identity of Indian villages and small towns is not confined to local markets. These products should reach other parts of the country and even global markets. Mr Modi said this also strengthens the Vocal for Local campaign and inspires the nation to become self-reliant. He added that the Vocal for Local mantra should not be forgotten during the upcoming festive season.Prime Minister Modi said the month of September is dedicated to the fight against malnutrition. During the Poshan Maah, individuals and organisations from various sectors come together for this noble cause. He said several commendable initiatives have been launched this year to combat malnutrition. Chhattisgarh has started the Har Ghar Munga – Ghar Ghar Munga (Moringa) campaign, under which people are being encouraged to include nutritious Moringa in their diet. Gujarat has also launched Vangi Spardha, a competition featuring dishes made from millets.This initiative promotes affordable and nutritious local cuisine. So far, more than two lakh people have participated in this contest. Maharashtra is also making commendable efforts in this direction, with teachers, Anganwadi workers, and parents joining awareness campaigns. In Mizoram, people have come together this year to launch a campaign for the upkeep of Poshan Vatikas.This aligns with the Mizo tradition of Talo-Mad-Yana, which signifies selfless service. Prime Minister Modi praised all such efforts, saying he is proud of everyone associated with Anganwadi centres that have been part of such initiatives. These Anganwadi centres are now digitally connected via the Poshan Tracker, with approximately nine crore beneficiaries registered on the platform.Mr Modi noted that the nation celebrated Ganesha Utsav this month with great devotion and enthusiasm. Giving the example of Panthoun Thirkhanon from Thailand, the Prime Minister said deep reverence for Him exists not only in India, but abroad as well. Lord Ganesha is worshipped as Phra Phikanet. When Panthoun Thirkhanon was 19 years old, his father gifted him a photograph of Lord Ganesha.With a profound sense of devotion awakened within, he spent over four decades studying traditions associated with Lord Ganesha. He has travelled across several Asian countries, including India and Nepal and has a special affection for Maharashtra. Through his efforts, the Ashtavinayak yatra has gained popularity among devotees in Thailand as well. In 2002, he established the Ganesha Himal Museum in Chiang Mai, northern Thailand.Today, it houses more than ten thousand idols of Lord Ganesha. The museum also has Ashtavinayak idols for devotees who are unable to travel to India. Worship rituals for Lord Ganesha are performed every Sunday morning around 10 o’clock.  Mr Modi said this demonstrates how India’s faith, art, and cultural traditions are gaining popularity in other countries as well.Concluding his address, Mr Modi urged listeners to keep sharing inspiring stories. He added that learning about these efforts through ‘Mann Ki Baat’ inspires people in other parts of the country as well. Extending his best wishes, the Prime Minister hoped that people would celebrate the upcoming festivals with joy and enthusiasm with family and friends.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices rebounded today. The Sensex rose 299 points or 0.4 per cent to close at 74,828. The Nifty jumped 118 points or half a per cent to settle at 23,447.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index climbed 0.7 per cent, while the Smallcap 100 index gained 0.9 per cent.

. In Men’s Cricket, the first One Day International of the 3-match series between India and West Indies will be played today at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. The match will start at 2 PM IST.Both Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli return to India’s ODI lineup after a two-month break from this format. Shubman Gill will lead Team India for this ODI series, while Shai Hope captains the West Indies.Akashvani correspondent reports the enthusiasm among cricket fans, which surged from the opening of ticket sales, has reached its peak with the arrival of both teams in Thiruvananthapuram. Cricket fans in the city are hoping to see India make a strong start in the opening match of the three-match ODI series.Tight security arrangements have been put in place at Thiruvananthapuram in connection with the India-West Indies match. Smithy M Palluruthy, Akashavani News, Thiruvananthapuram.”The second ODI will be played in Guwahati on September 30, followed by the third One Day International in New Chandigarh on October 3. The ODI series will be followed by five T20 internationals. The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) has proposed a major overhaul of the insurance distribution framework, including a simpler three-tier architecture, lower expense limits, revamped commission structures and stronger safeguards against mis-selling.The insurance regulator released a public consultation paper on “Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution”, outlining reforms covering distribution structure, expenses, commissions, market conduct, transparency and the use of digital infrastructure.Under the proposed norms, insurers and large distribution entities will have to disclose their commission policies and structures in a simple and accessible manner. Specified commercial policies will also carry commission disclosures, enabling customers to be aware of the distribution costs built into the pricing. The consultation paper also proposes tighter measures to curb mis-selling and compulsory bundling of insurance with other financial products.These include documenting customer needs and suitability, bringing direct and indirect remuneration within the regulatory definition of commission, and prohibiting volume-linked or reward-linked incentives for bank and Non-Banking Financial Company staff selling insurance. IRDAI has further proposed linking the identity of the individual seller with each policy, placing information on mis-selling incidents in the public domain and allowing commission claw-backs in cases of mis-selling.A key part of the proposed reforms is a reduction in insurers’ Expense of Management (EoM) limits. For life insurers, the EoM limit would shift to a company-level basis linked to Gross Direct Premium Income (GDPI), with the ceiling proposed at 15 per cent within two years and 12.5 per cent within five years. For general insurers, the calculation would shift from Gross Written Premium (GWP) to domestic GDPI, while the EoM limit would progressively decline from 30 per cent of GWP to 20 per cent of GDPI within five years.

The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. India has called upon all parties to exercise restraint, de-escalate tensions, ensure protection of civilians, and uninterrupted flow of energy and commerce during ongoing conflicts.Addressing the UN General Assembly in New York last night, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar pointed out that the repercussions of wars are experienced far outside the borders of directly engaged nations.He said hostilities continue to destabilise global security, threatening progress and slowing development far beyond their immediate regions.Dr Jaishankar said India is prepared to do everything possible to help improve the situation, particularly in the areas of food and energy security.Referring to the protracted Russia-Ukraine conflict, the minister said the ongoing war remains a critical international concern and echoed Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for an end to hostilities.On the Gulf conflict, Dr Jaishankar said the hostilities are exacerbating an already difficult situation.Turning to maritime security, he said attacks on commercial ships and seafarers in the Gulf and from the Red Sea to the Black Sea are unacceptable.External Affairs Minister also underscored the imperative of ensuring stable distribution channels for food grains and energy resources.Dr Jaishankar said that India will exercise its right to defend itself against terrorism. He called state-sponsored terrorism with a cross-border purpose a direct challenge to the global order.External Affairs Minister said governments engaged in such practices must be held accountable and the financing of terrorism must be exposed and countered.Dr Jaishankar said the world is witnessing weaponisation of everything, from finance and market access to supply chains and technology. He said countries are responding by reducing risks and diversifying their ties.Dr Jaishankar described a “4F crisis” confronting the Global South – the security of food, fuel, fertiliser and finance. He said India’s growth and public services have improved the prospects of one-sixth of humanity.He cited 600 major Indian development projects in 78 countries, spanning infrastructure, manufacturing, agriculture, information technology and capacity building.On artificial intelligence, Dr Jaishankar said, countries should be able to develop their own models and deployment plans in line with national priorities. He said India will make AI part of its partnership agenda with the Global South.External Affairs Minister said that countries should be free to develop artificial intelligence systems that serve their own priorities. He described AI as a tool that can empower people, support economic growth and help address challenges on a large scale.

India’s campaign for a permanent seat on the United Nations Security Council has received fresh support at the UN General Assembly, with Portugal and Mauritius explicitly backing New Delhi’s bid.The endorsements came during the 81st General Assembly debate at the UN headquarters in New York, amid broader calls for reforming the Security Council to better reflect current regional and political realities.Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro called for a more representative Security Council, including permanent membership for India.Mauritian Foreign Minister Dhananjay Ramful offered a direct endorsement in his address yesterday, saying Mauritius reiterated its support for India’s candidature for a permanent seat in recognition of its constructive role in global affairs.Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine also expressed indirect support for India through the G4 grouping, comprising India, Brazil, Germany and Japan.The Council currently has five permanent members with veto power – China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States – along with 10 elected members serving two-year terms.Any change to the Council’s composition requires approval by two-thirds of the General Assembly and ratification by two-thirds of UN member states, including all five permanent members.

. External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has emphasised the need to harness the possibilities offered by AI, anticipate its consequences and mitigate its risks. The Minister made these remarks while co-chairing an event on ‘AI in the Context of International Peace and Security, with an Emphasis on Maritime Security’, alongside Foreign Minister of Greece George Gerapetritis.During the event, Dr Jaishankar reaffirmed that AI and maritime security remain important priorities for India at the United Nations. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Bihar, East Madhya Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, West Bengal and North Eastern parts of the country during the next two days. IMD said that thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds are likely to prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Bihar, Jharkhand, Karnataka, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. Meanwhile, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Mahe are expected to experience hot and humid weather till 8th of this month.

. India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red color warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall along with thunderstorms and lightning over Uttarakhand today. Heavy to very heavy rainfall is also expected over Himachal Pradesh and West Uttar Pradesh.The IMD said heavy rainfall along with thunderstorms and lightning is also likely to prevail over Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Chandigarh, and Madhya Pradesh.Thunderstorms and lightning are also expected over Jammu, Kashmir, Ladakh, Gilgit, Baltistan, Muzaffarabad, Madhya Pradesh, and Punjab. Similar conditions are predicted over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Andhra Pradesh, East Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, Rajasthan and Telangana.Meanwhile, Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura are also likely to witness thunderstorms and lightning.
